title.narrative: Core Support Center for Analysis and Prevention of Corruption Moldova 2022-2025
Kärnstöd Center for Analysis and Prevention of Corruption Moldova 2022-2025

description.narrative: Detta bidrag är på väg att ge ett kärnstöd till CAPC 2022-2025 för genomförandet av den uppdragsdrivna institutionella CACP-strategin och RAF (Resultatbedömningsramverket). Organisationen kommer att få stöd för att genomföra kärnaktiviteter inom området för att bekämpa och förebygga korruption men också för att stärka interna institutionella policyer och processer för en hållbar och motståndskraftig utveckling.

This contribution is a about to grant a core support to CAPC in 2022-2025 for the implementation of the mission driven institutional CACP Strategy and RAF (Results Assessment Framework). The organisation will be supported to implement core activities in the field of combating and preventing corruption but also to strengthen internal institutional policies and processes for a sustainable and resilient development.

description.narrative:
CAPC created the prerequisites and laid the necessary foundations to achieve the main results of the project. So, for upgraded corruption proofing, monitoring and/or assessment tools, covering civic engagement and women empowerment, capitalized in partnerships with public and private sector CAPC started the review of corruption proofing tools and expertized the most relevant draft laws in the anti corruption field and justice. Special attention was paid to the analysis and mediatization of the situation in the field of anticorruption (through the preparation of an annual anti corruption report), as well as to collaboration with business associations. for achieving gender sensitive whistle blower reporting, protection and victim centered assistance in corruption cases provided, the foundations were laid for the creation of the assistance center for whistle blowers and victims of corruption, guidelines for victims of corruption were developed. At the same time, in 5 months of 2022, CAPC granted legal assistance to a whistle blower. As regards strengthened CAPC's organizational, expert, financial capacities, sustainability and visibility, CAPC strengthened CAPC's internal regulation by triggering the development of communication and fundraising strategies. At the same time, in order to improve internal processes, CAPC was audited from an environmental and gender perspective. The strengthening of technical and material capacities and of the CAPC team was achieved by organizing a team building of team members, experts and the CAPC Board of Directors and their participation in English courses.
Updates for 2023:
The CAPC has successfully advanced towards its strategic goals outlined in its Institutional Development and Capacity Strengthening Strategy for 2022-2025 by implementing several key initiatives: 1) Upgraded Corruption Proofing Tools: Review and Update: The CAPC reviewed and upgraded its methodology and electronic template for the corruption proofing of legislation, incorporating civic engagement and women empowerment perspectives. Workshop and Training: An updated electronic tool was presented to CAPC experts in a closed workshop, encouraging them to use the new tool for the corruption proofing of draft normative acts, considering human rights and environmental approaches. Expertise in Draft Laws: The CAPC provided expertise on significant draft laws in the anti-corruption and justice fields, adhering to the short deadlines set by national legislation. Annual Anti-Corruption Report: The CAPC prepared and presented an annual anti-corruption report to analyze and mediatize the anti-corruption landscape, fostering collaboration with business associations.
2) Gender-Sensitive Whistleblower Reporting and Victim Assistance: Assistance Centre: An assistance centre for whistleblowers and victims of corruption was established, offering guidelines and training for victims. Legal Assistance: In 2023, the CAPC provided legal assistance to two whistleblowers, demonstrating its commitment to victim-centred support.
3) Strengthened Organizational and Expert Capacities: Internal Regulation and Strategies: The CAPC developed communication and fundraising strategies to enhance internal regulations. Environmental and Gender Audit: Internal processes were audited from an environmental and gender perspective, ensuring sustainable and inclusive practices. Team Building and Training: Technical and material capacities were strengthened through team-building activities and English courses for team members, experts, and the Board of Directors.
Lessons Learned: Objective Planning: Clear objectives ensure smooth activity execution and consistent instruction for duty-bearers and stakeholders. Discussions and preparations are crucial for shared understanding and desired outcomes. Professional Communication: Timely, professional communication is vital for achieving positive results. Skilled negotiation is necessary to maintain high-quality organizational outputs. Flexible Partnerships: Building effective partnerships requires adapting to partners' needs and being flexible in strategy development. A strong portfolio of activities by recognized experts enhances partnership efficacy. By adhering to these lessons, the CAPC can continue to improve its processes, expand its impact, and maintain its commitment to anti-corruption efforts and capacity building.
Updates 2024: In 2024, the Centre for the Analysis and Prevention of Corruption (CAPC) in Moldova achieved significant progress in advancing its mission to strengthen anti-corruption mechanisms, promote transparency, and build institutional resilience. The year was marked by both the fulfilment of expected objectives and the emergence of several impactful, unanticipated outcomes, which together underscore the organizations growing influence and maturity.
One of the core areas of achievement was the rigorous analysis of draft legislation. CAPC resumed and enhanced its expertise in corruption proofing of normative acts, incorporating a newly integrated Methodology that aligns anti-corruption principles with human rights-based approaches. A total of 67 draft laws were reviewed using a refined electronic template that enabled a dual focus on qualitative and quantitative risks. These acts, mostly initiated by the Government and dealing with justice, constitutional matters, and administration, were systematically assessed and shared with parliamentary committees. CAPC ensured transparency by publishing the findings online and disseminating them widely through media and social platforms.
In parallel, CAPC continued to build public accountability through an expanded portfolio of monitoring and assessment tools. Reports developed in 2024 spanned a wide range of critical areas, including judicial vetting processes, decision-making transparency, and procurement practices. Notably, the 2023 Anti-Corruption Report and the analysis of parliamentary oversight in 20222023 provided a comprehensive view of Moldovas anti-corruption landscape. These reports not only documented systemic challenges but also delivered detailed, evidence-based recommendations for reform. A suite of seven procurement-focused reports further deepened CAPCs scrutiny at both national and regional levels, with a special emphasis on education, health, and food safety sectors.
A particularly visible achievement was the "#BaniCurati" anti-corruption campaign, launched to raise awareness and drive behavioural change within Moldovas business community. What began as a targeted campaign evolved into a multi-channel national initiative, blending creative communication with strategic policy messaging. Digital billboards featuring cultural icons, influencer-led social media engagement, and televised interviews amplified the campaigns impact. CAPC also supported small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) by producing tailored anti-bribery guidance, legal resources, and training materials. These efforts culminated in over 846,000 views on CAPCs Facebook page during the campaigns peak, and a marked increase in both online engagement and public discourse on corruption in the private sector.
In the area of whistleblower protection, CAPC made significant headway. Building on Moldovas new Whistleblower Protection Law, CAPC provided legal support in high-profile cases and organized regional training sessions for SMEs. The organization also produced accessible video content and infographics explaining the rights of whistleblowers and how to seek support. A particularly successful outreach initiative was a sketch-comedy style video spot that aired across 18 national and regional outlets, reaching approximately 915,000 viewers. This helped normalize public interest disclosures and challenge the stigma surrounding whistleblowing, especially in high-risk sectors such as education and healthcare.
Perhaps one of the most transformative areas of impact was CAPCs internal development. In 2024, the organization underwent a mid-term evaluation of its Institutional Development Strategy and Action Plan, which served as both a moment of reflection and a catalyst for further growth. The findings and recommendations of the evaluation were reviewed during a strategic workshop in May, where the team explored improvements in governance, fundraising, and visibility. As a result, CAPC launched three marketable service packages: one supporting ISO 37001 implementation, another offering legislative harmonization services, and a third focused on whistleblower protection. These services not only diversify CAPCs funding base but also position the organization as a provider of expert anti-corruption support across sectors.
CAPC also invested in building its human capital. The team participated in training on gender mainstreaming, legislative harmonization, and the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) protection mechanisms for whistleblowers. Two international study visitsto the ECHR in Strasbourg and to the Romanian Academic Society in Bucharest broadened CAPCs strategic vision and fostered valuable cross-border learning. The discussions in Bucharest, in particular, helped clarify the role of civil society organizations in both pre- and post-EU accession contexts, directly informing CAPCs long-term strategic positioning.
On the communications front, the organization reaped the benefits of implementing its 2023 Communication Strategy and Brand Book. CAPCs online presence expanded significantly: its website traffic quadrupled to nearly 54,000 page views, and its social media following grew by 15%. Notably, the organization launched an Instagram page to connect with younger audiences and produced branded visibility materials such as T-shirts, backpacks, and umbrellas that helped reinforce its public identity.
In addition to planned outputs, several unexpected outcomes enriched CAPCs overall impact. Informal support networks developed among trained stakeholders, sustaining motivation and knowledge-sharing well beyond the initial sessions. CAPCs research and reports began to influence policy debates at higher levels, a positive sign of increasing credibility and reach. Moreover, the visibility and engagement from the "#BaniCurati" campaign far exceeded expectations, proving the power of well-executed public communication in shaping attitudes and behaviours.
